sections.content:
215,405 people

were counted on the census as "carpenters and joiners" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Carpenters and joiners construct, erect, install and repair wooden structures and fittings used in internal and external frameworks and cut, shape, fit and assemble wood to make templates, jigs, scale models and scenic equipment for theatres.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "carpenters and joiners" there were more men than women (98.8% compared with 1.2%).

This means "carpenters and joiners" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled construction and building trades".

Men made up 98.8% and women made up 1.2% of "carpenters and joiners"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "carpenters and joiners" included:

  • pipe fitters
  • plasterers
  • plumbers and heating and ventilating installers and repairers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "carpenters and joiners" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "carpenters and joiners", 12.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "carpenters and joiners" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "carpenters and joiners" included:

  • plumbers and heating and ventilating installers and repairers
  • welding trades
  • elementary process plant occupations (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "carpenters and joiners" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of men than women with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "carpenters and joiners" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "carpenters and joiners", 7.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (86.2% compared with 13.8%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (66%) than an employee (34%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the region of the South West.
